_what_this_is: A structural negative result about the OUTER level on this seed, measured before any candidate was accepted. Recorded per Rule 5 (first-class negative results).
_finding: Every per-type and per-question calibration family is ARGMAX-INVARIANT on this architecture, so none of them can move the decision metric the accept rule tests.
_why: All candidates within one question share that question's type. A per-type map is therefore a SINGLE affine (or temperature) transform applied to every candidate of that question, which is monotone, and a monotone map cannot change an argmax. This is a property of the head -- one scalar score per candidate -- and not of any particular stage's fitting.

_evidence.reading: the three per-type scales are exactly invariant; the per-candidate perturbation moves the score. The difference between the two blocks is non-monotonicity WITHIN a question, and it is the only difference.

_stages_measured_on_medium.note: five stages, five different calibration behaviours, one identical accuracy. The axis that differs most (ECE 0.3715 -> 0.0408, a 9x spread) is the axis the accept rule does not read.

_what_it_means_for_the_loop: Under the ecosystem's accept rule (single declared metric = accuracy, single threshold), all five are TIED and rejected. That is the rule working correctly, and it is also a finding: the dominant calibration lever on this seed cannot reach the decision metric. Reaching it requires a stage whose parameters vary BY CANDIDATE within a question.

_ecosystem_comparison.cygnet_official_rank_1: Cygnet, blockbrain, frozen gemma-4-12B-it, capability 79.0, 203/231 = 87.9% on JevBench public. NO fine-tuning; one calibration temperature T=3.4 fitted by NLL on self-generated items.
_ecosystem_comparison.why_its_temperature_moves_the_argmax_and: Cygnet maps each option to a LETTER and reads that letter token's probability at the answer position. The options are then DIFFERENT TOKENS, so a temperature reshapes their probabilities non-monotonically. Our head emits one scalar per candidate, so a per-type or per-question temperature acts on the candidate axis homogeneously and cannot reorder them.
_ecosystem_comparison.transferable: The one-token-per-decision readout is what makes a scalar temperature a first-class lever rather than a monotone no-op. It is a property of the READOUT, not of the model, and it is the specific mechanism this project lacks.

_not_a_claim: That no harness can move accuracy on this seed. Only that the per-type and per-question families cannot, and that the measured per-candidate perturbation can.
